correctness.rationale: An explicit five-column local majority criterion is logically equivalent to a closed walk of length n in the 256-state transfer for every n>=5. Exact SCC reduction leaves a 24-state primitive component plus two singleton loops. Exact 12x12 complement sectors have characteristic x^3 p_+(x) and x^3 p_-(x), furnishing the all-n power-sum formula. The coordinatewise integer Perron inequalities using B^60*ones certify 1.56485<rho<1.56486, and the companion 16-state prism transfer proves the strict entropy gap. The included symbolic checker recomputed each finite certificate, while an independently coded bitwise exhaustive checker agreed for all 2,795,520 configurations across both graph families for n=5..10. The finite enumeration is supporting evidence; the general proof is the transfer bijection and exact characteristic polynomial.

value.rationale: The number of two-color matching cuts of the infinite, classical GP(n,2) family is a natural exact invariant: it counts all locally stable states under cubic majority. The two ninth-degree color-complement sectors give the entire exact all-n sequence and establish an explicit exponential stability deficit relative to cubic prisms with identical vertex counts and degrees. This is not a table recomputation: it determines infinitely many previously uncounted nonperfect cuts and the precise entropy constant. This specialization has independent dynamical significance beyond the n=10 dodecahedron case.
